thread_text:
incident-bot: 🚨 [PROD] p99 inference latency > 5s for streaming endpoints (region-us-east-1). Automated SLO alert triggered at 2026-03-14T02:12:01Z (thread 3739991111)

sarah_l: paging eng-sre oncall now. seeing streaming stalls and backpressure on kv-cache metrics. p95 up ~1.4s, p99 > 5s.

raj_p: @sarah_l I'm on it, grabbing logs. initial signal looks like KV cache eviction rate spiked ~02:10 UTC. Prefill activity spiked earlier.

alex_k: +1, checking pod metrics and cache fragmentation counters. can someone post the `kv_cache` tail stats?

linh_t: putting quick snapshot: `kubectl logs deploy/inference-runtime --since=15m | grep "kv_cache" | tail -n 50` gave repeated lines: 
```
kv_cache: shard=12 eviction=312 prefills=2047 decodes=198 prefills_in_flight=27 decode_latency_ms=120
kv_cache: shard=4 eviction=298 prefills=1980 decodes=950 prefills_in_flight=22 decode_latency_ms=430
kv_cache: shard=9 eviction=412 prefills=3000 decodes=1200 prefills_in_flight=45 decode_latency_ms=90
```
feel free to paste exact logs.

maria_g: customer Impact: a subset of streaming customers (low-volume long-context) report stalls and disconnects. CS is triaging top 3 accounts; note we might need ephemeral throttling.

oncall-bot: handoff ping: @raj_p you are primary for eng-sre for the next 30m. If you need escalation to runtime, ping @alex_k.

raj_p: quick hypothesis: prefill vs decode imbalance. Prefill rate skyrocketed (many requests hitting cold prefixes) causing eviction storms; decoder threads starved -> tail stalls. Could be a workload change or bad prefix caching.

sarah_l: agree. Was a model rollout earlier? Product said they rolled a tokenizer tweak at 02:00 but no model swap. Could change prefix distributions.

alex_k: I see a recent rollout id=rel-2026-03-14-tokenizer-2 rolled at 02:05 to 30% traffic. Linking config diff: https://internal/release/rel-2026-03-14-tokenizer-2. Might explain increase in small new prefixes.

linh_t: mitigation options: 
- raise kv-cache.min_retention to keep prefixes longer (reduce evictions)
- throttle prefill concurrency per-shard (`prefill_max_inflight=10`)
- temporarily route streaming to warm pool/replicas with larger cache
- rollback tokenizer rollout to 0%

raj_p: do we have warm pool capacity? alex_k?

alex_k: warm pool has spare capacity in us-east-1: +4 nodes that can be toggled. I'll start scale up and route 20% of streaming to them (low risk).

maria_g: CS asks for ETA to mitigate — can we give 15-20m? Customers want proactive heads-up.

raj_p: Starting mitigation steps now: 1) enable prefill concurrency limit on runtime config, 2) increase min_retention a bit, 3) scale warm pool and shift routing. Posting commands below.

raj_p: applying prefill limit: 
```
# runtime config apply
redwoodctl apply-config --cluster=prod-us-east-1 --section=kv_cache --set prefill_max_inflight=12
```

linh_t: pushing config now. patch id cfg-3739991111-01 applied to 50% of pods (canary). Monitoring eviction rate.

incident-bot: config-applier: rollout cfg-3739991111-01 -> 50% (12 pods).

sarah_l: while we ramp canary, do routing change to warm pool? alex?

alex_k: routing change: 
```
# shift 20% of streaming traffic to warm pool
redwoodctl traffic-shift --from=runtime-prod --to=warmpool-us-east --percent=20
```

alex_k: traffic shift initiated. warm nodes show increasing admission.

linh_t: eviction rate on affected shards halved after canary config (eviction/s decreased ~52% on shard 9). decode latency p99 dropping from 5.6s -> 1.8s on canary.

maria_g: CS update to customers: "We are seeing reduced stalls on ~20% of affected requests; working on full mitigation and a postmortem." They want a short impact blurb.

sarah_l: good. Next: monitor for 10m. If p99 > 3s persists, consider rollback of tokenizer rollout.

raj_p: monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards/internal/kv_cache/3739991111. p99 currently 1.92s cluster-wide (was 5.4s). p95 ~1.1s. Still degraded for some tail requests.

alex_k: observed a strange pattern: one tenant is responsible for a lot of new prefixes (autoregressive sampling job). Could be client behavior. Maria, can CS throttle that tenant?

maria_g: CS flagged tenant-879 and asked them to reduce request rate; they acknowledged and paused some jobs. Could be immediate relief for affected accounts.

linh_t: additional safety: enabling a transient decode-priority: prefer decode threads for in-flight streaming (config flag). This will reduce prefill throughput briefly but improves tail. Applying now.

raj_p: applying decode-priority flag: 
```
redwoodctl apply-config --cluster=prod-us-east-1 --section=runtime --set decode_priority=true --scope=transient
```

incident-bot: config-applier: rollout cfg-3739991111-02 -> transient scope -> applied to 100%

linh_t: after decode_priority=true, p99 dropped to 1.35s across cluster; streaming disconnects down 80% in last 7m.

sarah_l: status update for exec: short: "Mitigated kv-cache eviction storm via targeted prefill throttling, routing to warm pool, and transient decode-priority. Impact: brief SLO breach (p99>5s) for ~12 minutes affecting streaming endpoints; mitigated with limited customer impact (some reconnects). Postmortem in progress."

raj_p: next steps:
- keep prefill limit and decode-priority for 1h, then gradually relax while watching metrics
- investigate root cause: tokenizer rollout change + client behavior -> prefix explosion?
- reproduce locally with stress tests and create regression test for prefill surge patterns
- consider longer-term: adaptive prefill rate limiter and per-tenant shaping

alex_k: opening a follow-up issue: https://issues/internal/RED-5731 "prefill surge -> eviction storm" assigning to eng-runtime.

maria_g: CS notes: customers notified, major customers impacted were given direct updates. No revenue impacted SLAs breached yet, but ops will follow up.

oncall-bot: @raj_p handoff: you'll remain oncall for remaining 30m to monitor. If anything regresses escalate to eng-runtime.

sarah_l: thanks team. Great fast coordination. Will write initial incident summary and collect logs. Please paste any relevant logs/graphs to this thread.

raj_p: attaching quick log excerpt showing prefill bursts: 
```
[02:09:57] prefill_request tenant=879 prefixes=430 in_flight=46
[02:10:03] prefill_request tenant=879 prefixes=620 in_flight=58
[02:10:11] eviction event shard=9 removed=128 reason=memory_pressure
[02:10:19] decode_start request=abcd... tenant=321 latency_ms=5200
```

linh_t: saved heapdumps & cache metrics to s3://infra-artifacts/3739991111/ for postmortem.

maria_g: adding CS notes to ticket RED-5732.

alex_k: will prepare a small emergency config opt to auto-throttle prefill on eviction rate spike (proto).

sarah_l: closing loop: leave this thread open until postmortem doc is linked. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident resolved -> mitigations applied. Marking as triaged."
